To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an algorithm to identify relevant sub-spaces of interest on social media for monitoring drug consumption, and that we have applied our method to study the opioid epidemic in the US.

we present an information retrieval algorithm that can identify relevant subspaces for mining data from social media, that almost 1.6 million Reddit users are geolocated and show interest in discussions about opiate consumption and that we provide a domain specific lexicon for the opioid epidemic.

we have developed an algorithm to identify users interested in opioid consumption in Reddit, that we have estimated the prevalence of such interest in the US at the state level with a novel indicator, and that we have extracted a domain specific vocabulary that can be used in digital public health surveillance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methodologies to monitor and characterize the opioid epidemic through a digital cohort.
the identification of a digital cohort of interest in the opioid consumption, the estimation of a prevalence of interest at the state level and the development of a domain specific vocabulary.
the development of novel computational methodologies for the extraction of signals on social media that are relevant for public health surveillance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our methodology is able to provide a complementary view to the official statistics, and it might be used as a digital epidemiology tool for monitoring the opioid crisis.

this work represents an important step in developing new methods and techniques for the analysis and interpretation of social media data, and for the development of new indicators of public health interest.
this paper presents a computational approach to monitor the opioid epidemic through a digital cohort of users showing explicit interest on the topic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are proposing a novel methodology to monitor the opioid epidemic through social media.
the opioid epidemic is a complex and multifaceted issue that requires the use of multiple data sources and methodologies to be fully understood and addressed.
we have developed a novel methodology that can be applied to a variety of social media platforms, and can be used to extract novel insights about public health phenomena.
The main takeaway from our work is that

digital epidemiology can provide a novel lens on the opioid crisis that can be complementary to traditional surveillance and can provide new information that is not encoded in the official statistics.
digital epidemiology can provide complementary information to traditional public health surveillance.

digital cohorts of social media users can be leveraged for public health surveillance, providing a novel view on the opioid epidemic that can be used to complement and improve existing public health surveillance.
